A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the development of prosociality in emerging adulthood is influenced by a temperamental dimension (effortful control) and a personality factor (ego-resiliency) that are both present in adolescence and are relatively stable across development.

the development of prosociality during the transition from late adolescence to young adulthood is predicted by a temperamental dimension (i.e., effortful control) indirectly via the mediation of a personality factor (ego-resiliency).
the development of prosociality is influenced by the interaction of temperamental and personality factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the development of prosociality is influenced by the interaction between temperament and personality, and that the promotion of prosociality requires a comprehensive intervention strategy aimed at enhancing the capacity to cope with emotional reactions and to deal with challenging social situations.
